correctness.rationale: For Cr_n=K_{n,n} minus a perfect matching, distance-two pairs are precisely same-bipartition distinct-index pairs. At most one red-isolated vertex per side, so >=n-1 red edges; equality forces a matching omitting one vertex each. If omitted indices differ a same-side pair has no rainbow geodesic, hence both are same s. The n-1 matching corresponds to a permutation of [n]\{s} with no fixed points (graph has missing diagonal); a two-cycle creates an unavailable pair of red intermediates, and conversely absence of 2-cycles makes all same-side pairs have an available red-blue two-step route. EGF for permutations with cycles length>=3 is exp(-z-z^2/2)/(1-z); n choices s gives n*a_{n-1}. At n=3 Cr_3 is C6; two alternating colorings, three red edges. Independently enumerated every subset of red edges through the first feasible cardinality for n=3,4,5, recovering min/count (3,2),(3,8),(4,30); evaluated the n=6..8 constructor and code scope separately. This is not full rainbow connection of diameter-three matched pairs.
